result.stderr:
parsley v3.2.0.0

An advanced LL parser synthesizer for C#

Usage: parsley [<grammar-file>] [--lexer <lexer-file>] [--output <code-file>]
        [--shared] [--base] [--engine <engine>] [--report] [--no-lines]

    <grammar-file>            The path to the XBNF grammar input file. Defaults
                              to <stdin>.
    -l, --lexer <lexer-file>  The lexer output file to generate. Terminals from
                              other lexers (lexer=Name) go in files beside it,
                              named like grammar.Name.lex.
    -o, --output <code-file>  The path to the ouput code file. Defaults to
                              <stdout>.
    -s, --shared              Generate the shared runtime: ParsleyRuntime.cs
                              and the parser base class for the grammar's
                              engine.
    -b, --base                Generate only the parser base class for the
                              grammar's engine (LL1ParserBase.cs,
                              LLkParserBase.cs or AllStarParserBase.cs), for a
                              project that already has ParsleyRuntime.cs.
    -e, --engine <engine>     The parsing engine: auto (the lightest the
                              grammar allows), ll1, llk or allstar. Defaults to
                              auto.
    -r, --report              Write a report on the grammar to <stdout> instead
                              of a parser: the engine it needs and why, its
                              decisions and lookahead, and the size of the
                              synthesized code.
    -n, --no-lines            Omit the #line directives that map the generated
                              code back to the grammar. Compiler errors and the
                              debugger then point at the generated C#, and C#
                              IntelliSense in semantic actions can't find the
                              code.
